about: Election Desk 2026 is a live desk for the midterms. The map drills from the country to the states to every county, colored by the race ratings, the polls, the prediction markets, the early vote or the 2024 presidential vote before Election Day, and by the results after the polls close. Click a state for its races, candidates, polls, early-vote totals and largest counties.

Ratings are from the Cook Political Report, Sabato’s Crystal Ball and Inside Elections, as of the dates each shows; the map uses their consensus. Poll averages name their aggregator. Early-vote figures come from the UF Election Lab and state election offices and are party registration, not vote choice. Market prices are from Kalshi and Polymarket. County baselines are the certified 2024 and 2020 presidential votes. On election night, results carry the time they were read and the source; a check mark is a call by the Associated Press or the source named, never this page’s own.

The page is rebuilt by an automated updater: a scheduled run reads the feeds and the results pages, writes the data files and republishes, every morning until Election Day and then continuously; the page refetches its data while open. The forecast probabilities are from The Hinge, hosted next door.

primarySource.name: UF Election Lab 2026 Early Voting tracker (Michael McDonald)
primarySource.updateCadence: Intraday as states post; page showed 'Last updated: Oct 23, 2026 @ 3:25pm Eastern Time' and later '@ 5:44pm Eastern Time' on the same day. Some states do not provide daily updates; the 'updates_today' column counts how many times a state was refreshed that day; 'last_update' is per state (M/D/YYYY).
primarySource.notes: The national page is a JavaScript dashboard: a plain HTTP fetch of the HTML shows placeholder 'X' values. All numbers come from one CSV, /data-downloads/earlyvote/2026/US.csv (one row per state + DC, 49 rows on 2026-10-23: no AL or NH rows). Columns: state,state_abbv,turn_2022,last_update,data_source,notes,request_*,accept_*,inperson_*,voted_* (each with _all,_dem,_rep,_none, age_1..4, nh_white/nh_black/nh_asian/nh_native_american/nh_other/hispanic, male/female/gender_unknown) and updates_today. voted_all = total early votes; accept_all = mail ballots returned; inperson_all = in-person early votes; request_all = mail ballots requested (for all-mail states this is active registrants or ballots issued; see per-state notes). National totals on the page equal the column sums of US.csv (verified: 23,590,165 / 10,787,246 / 12,802,919 / 59,216,745). Party figures are voter registration, only for states with party registration (27 states on 10/23). Per-state pages exist at /early-vote/2026-early-voting/2026-general-election-early-vote-{state-slug}/ for 32 states (linked from the national page) and load {ST}_county.csv, {ST}_cd.csv, {ST}_sdl.csv, {ST}_sdu.csv from the same /data-downloads/earlyvote/2026/ folder; house_tossup_races.csv is also there. Directory listing is forbidden (403); {ST}.csv does not exist (404). The 2024 final file is at /data-downloads/earlyvote/2024/US.csv (same layout, turn_2020 column); /2022/US.csv returns 404 (2022 tracker lived on RPubs). License: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 - attribution required, no commercial use without permission. Fields with 0 mean 'not published/not applicable' as often as 'zero'.
primarySource.scriptHint: GET https://election.lab.ufl.edu/data-downloads/earlyvote/2026/US.csv once or twice daily (cache-bust with a query string); parse CSV; sum voted_all/accept_all/inperson_all/request_all for national; per state use voted_all, accept_all, inperson_all, request_all, voted_dem/voted_rep/voted_none, last_update, updates_today.

comparison.text: The UF 2026 page publishes no same-point 2022 or 2024 comparison text; it offers a map option '2026 Early Vote to 2022 Total Turnout Ratio' (early votes divided by each state's total 2022 turnout, the turn_2022 column). Final 2024 early+mail total across the 49 UF-tracked jurisdictions = sum of voted_all in the archived 2024 US.csv. AP (via Fox 10 Phoenix, 2026-10-17) reported about 6 million early/mail ballots cast across 39 states as of Thursday Oct 15, 2026; no 2022 comparison given. Michigan SOS press release of 2026-10-06 is titled 'Four weeks before Election Day, mail ballot returns are up 30% over same point in 2022' (title only; body not fetched).

GA.notes: UF note: Georgia's county-level "Ballots Issued and Accepted" and "Ballots to Date" downloads (from the state's election-data-hub dashboard, https://sos.ga.gov/page/election-data-hub-unofficial-turnout) are compared against the statewide absentee file, county by county, using whichever is higher - this is how same-day in-person early-voting activity (which the statewide absentee file doesn't carry until the next overnight refresh) gets folded in. No district or demographic breakdown is available from these county-level downloads. Early in-person voting dates from Atlanta News First (2026-10-19) citing Georgia SOS: opened Oct 13, runs through Oct 30; Election Day Nov 3. GA SOS reported 1,005,130 total ballots (960,707 in person) as of 5:50 p.m. Oct 19.

headlines.text: UF Election Lab tracker: 24,274,661 early votes nationally (10,917,370 in person, 13,357,291 mail ballots returned, 59,332,375 requested) across 48 reporting states/DC, per the CSV pulled at 08:15 UTC Oct 24; up 684,496 from the Oct 23 5:44 p.m. ET reading.
UF Election Lab tracker shows 23,590,165 early votes nationally (10,787,246 in person, 12,802,919 mail returned, 59,216,745 mail ballots requested) across 47 reporting states/DC as of 5:44 p.m. ET.
Texas leads all states with 2,858,285 early votes (2,735,900 in person) per UF Election Lab; California 2,478,771 (all mail), Florida 2,285,310, Georgia 1,613,269, North Carolina 1,269,920.
Georgia passed 1 million ballots cast (1,005,130 total, 960,707 in person) as of 5:50 p.m. Oct 19, six days into early voting that runs Oct 13-30.
Georgia's first day of early in-person voting drew more than 190,000 voters, over 53,000 above the first-day total in 2022, per the Georgia Secretary of State's office.

AP counted about 6 million early and mail ballots cast across 39 states as of Thursday Oct 15; California (757,000+), Florida (~669,000), Virginia (604,000+), Michigan (~573,000) and Pennsylvania (391,000+) led.
Michigan SOS press release: 'Four weeks before Election Day, mail ballot returns are up 30% over same point in 2022' (headline figure; release body not fetched).

calendar.text: Georgia advance (early) in-person voting began; runs through the Friday before Election Day (Oct 30, per statute).
calendar.source: https://georgia.gov/node/34066 (fetched 2026-10-23: 'starting October 13, 2026'); end date from O.C.G.A. 21-2-385 (prior knowledge)

calendar.text: North Carolina one-stop early voting began (third Thursday before Election Day); same-day registration available at early-voting sites.
Nevada early voting began (third Saturday before Election Day).
Texas early voting began.
Alaska early voting began (15 days before Election Day). Florida counties could begin optional early voting (15th day before).
Wisconsin in-person absentee voting may begin (14 days before; municipal schedules vary).
Texas deadline for counties to receive mail-ballot applications.
Florida mandatory early-voting period begins (10th day before; through Oct 31, counties may extend through Nov 1). Michigan's statewide nine-day early voting period begins (through Nov 1).
Pennsylvania deadline to apply for a mail-in or absentee ballot (5pm; first Tuesday before Election Day).
Maine: last day to request/vote an absentee ballot in person without special circumstances (third business day before the election).
Texas early voting ends.
Early voting ends in Georgia (Friday before), Arizona (7pm Friday before) and Nevada (Friday before).
Early voting ends in North Carolina (3pm, last Saturday before), Virginia (Saturday before) and the mandatory Florida period (counties may run through Nov 1).
calendar.source: N.C.G.S. 163-227.2; Va. Code 24.2-701.1; Fla. Stat. 101.657 (prior knowledge)

calendar.text: Early voting ends in Michigan (Sunday before), Ohio (in-person early voting, Sunday 5pm) and Wisconsin (in-person absentee, Sunday before). Daylight saving time ends; Election Day closing times below are standard time.
calendar.source: MCL 168.720a; Ohio R.C. 3509.051; Wis. Stat. 6.86 (prior knowledge)

calendar.text: In-person early/absentee voting ends in Iowa (Monday before), Kansas (advance voting ends noon) and Minnesota (5pm).
calendar.source: Iowa Code 53.10; K.S.A. 25-1122; Minn. Stat. 203B.081 (prior knowledge)

calendar.text: Election Day. Same-day voter registration is available on Election Day in about 22 states plus DC (including CA, CO, CT, HI, ID, IL, IA, ME, MD, MI, MN, MT, NV, NH, NM, UT, VT, VA, WA, WI, WY); North Carolina allows it only during early voting.
calendar.source: NCSL same-day registration table (prior knowledge; not fetched)

calendar.text: Polls close 6:00pm ET: Kentucky (eastern zone; western zone 7:00pm ET). Indiana eastern zone also 6:00pm ET (no Senate/governor race).
Polls close 7:00pm ET: Georgia, South Carolina, Virginia, Vermont, Florida (eastern zone), Kentucky (western zone).
Polls close 7:30pm ET: North Carolina, Ohio, West Virginia.

Polls close 8:00pm ET: Alabama, Connecticut, Delaware, Florida (Panhandle), Illinois, Kansas (central zone), Maine, Maryland, Massachusetts, Michigan (eastern zone), Mississippi, New Hampshire (latest; most towns 7:00pm), New Jersey, Oklahoma, Pennsylvania, Rhode Island, South Dakota (central zone), Tennessee (both zones), Texas (central zone); 8:30pm ET: Arkansas.

Polls close 9:00pm ET: Arizona, Colorado, Iowa, Kansas (mountain zone), Louisiana, Michigan (Upper Peninsula central zone), Minnesota, Nebraska (both zones), New Mexico, New York, South Dakota (mountain zone), Texas (El Paso/Hudspeth), Wisconsin, Wyoming.

Polls close 10:00pm ET: Idaho (mountain zone), Montana, Nevada, Oregon (Malheur County). 11:00pm ET: California, Idaho (Pacific zone), Oregon (Pacific zone). 12:00am ET Nov 4: Alaska (Alaska zone), Hawaii. 1:00am ET Nov 4: Alaska (Aleutians).
Texas: deadline (5pm) to receive mail ballots postmarked by Election Day. Counting continues in CA, NV, OR, AZ (late early ballots), PA, MI, WI; Alaska and Maine ranked-choice tabulations pending.
Receipt deadlines for mail ballots postmarked by Election Day: Kansas (3 days), Massachusetts (5pm, 3rd day), Virginia (noon, 3rd day).
calendar.source: K.S.A. 25-1132; M.G.L. c.54 s.95; Va. Code 24.2-709 (prior knowledge)

calendar.text: Nevada: 5pm deadline to receive mail ballots postmarked by Election Day. Ohio: deadline to receive absentee ballots postmarked by Nov 2 (4th day after).
calendar.source: NRS 293.269921; Ohio R.C. 3509.05 as amended by HB 458 (prior knowledge)

calendar.text: Georgia: county certification deadline (5pm, Monday after Election Day). New Jersey: receipt deadline for mail ballots postmarked by Election Day (6 days).
calendar.source: O.C.G.A. 21-2-493(k) as amended by SB 202; N.J.S.A. 19:63-22 (prior knowledge)

Georgia general-election runoff (Senate, governor and other races) if no candidate exceeds 50% on Nov 3 - four weeks after the general election under current law.
